part.text:
All done. The implementation is complete in `src/lib.rs` — all 9 tests pass (including the `#[ignore]`d ones) and clippy is clean.

## What I built

The module tree matches the test imports: `dot_dsl::graph::Graph`, `dot_dsl::graph::graph_items::node::Node`, and `dot_dsl::graph::graph_items::edge::Edge`.

- **`Node`** — `name: String` plus `attrs: HashMap<String, String>`, with `new(name)`, `with_attrs(...)`, and `attr(name) -> Option<&str>`.
- **`Edge`** — `from`/`to` endpoints plus the same `attrs` map and methods.
- **`Graph`** — public `nodes`, `edges`, and `attrs` fields (the tests read them directly), with builder methods `with_nodes`, `with_edges`, `with_attrs`, and a `node(name) -> Option<&Node>` lookup.

## Builder pattern details

- All `with_*` methods take `&self`, clone, mutate, and return the new value — so calls chain fluently (`Graph::new().with_nodes(...).with_edges(...).with_attrs(...)`) and the original is never consumed.
- `new` methods are generic over `K: AsRef<str>` so they accept `&str`, `String`, or even `&&str` (as in the `graph_nodes_store_attributes` test).
- The tricky part was `with_attrs`: the tests call it with both `&[("color", "green")]` (tuples by value) and `&[attr]` where `attr: &(&str, &str)` (references to tuples). A single bound `P: Borrow<(&'a str, &'b str)>` handles both, since `T: Borrow<T>` holds reflexively for values and `&T: Borrow<T>` for references. A shared private `insert_attrs` helper in `lib.rs` does the actual `HashMap` population for all three types.

No new files or dependencies were needed, and the tests and build files were left untouched.
